newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-STRUGGLING FOREST MOVE TOWARDS TAKEOVER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRUGGLING FOREST MOVE TOWARDS TAKEOVER.

text.p: Nottingham Forest's shareholders gave the go-ahead at their annual meeting on Thursday for the board of directors to continue talks into a takeover of the struggling English premier league club.

Two consortiums, one headed by video tycoon Grant Bovey and the other by former Tottenham Hotspur chairman Irving Scholar, are believed to have tabled packages worth 30 million pounds sterling ($48.85 million) to take control of the club.
Irving Korn, who ousted Fred Reacher as chairman, said: "The shareholders have given us a mandate to continue to look at the proposals we have had and others that may still arrive.
"With the help of our financial advisors we will prepare a report to go to an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders in the coming weeks.
"I believe a takeover is the way ahead and, judging by the reaction of shareholders, they appear to feel the same way."

Korn denied there was any rift between him and Reacher, who commented: "The chairmanship issue was a democratic decision and Irving will get the same support from me as he has given over the last four years."
On the field, Forest are enduring wretched form. They have not won in 10 premier league matches since the opening day of the season.
